bypassPermissions.label: Bypass
bypassPermissions.description: Skips every approval AND the sandbox (containers/VMs only)

busyMarker.source: Live capture of a working codex pane (codex-cli 0.154.0, gpt-6-astra): the status row renders `• Working (23s • esc to interrupt)`. `esc to interrupt` is the stable half of that line; the elapsed seconds change every tick. NOT sufficient alone here — codex keeps its composer drawn mid-turn, which is why `idleMarker` is also set. Key bindings are user-configurable, so a rebound interrupt key would change this string; that is a known limit of every marker in this block, not a defect of this one.

promptPattern.source: Live capture. An EMPTY codex composer is not a bare glyph — it draws the glyph, a separator, then the dim placeholder `Ask Codex to do anything`. Matching the placeholder is a POSITIVE test for a bare prompt: typing replaces it, so a half-typed line stops matching, and a dialog row (`› 1. Yes, continue`, seen on the directory-trust prompt) never matches. Two things were measured rather than assumed. The line cannot be end-anchored: codex draws an animated braille shimmer across it, so it rarely ends at the placeholder. And the separator cell is not reliably a space — the shimmer OVERWRITES it, observed live as `›⠁Ask Codex to do anything⡁`, so the class accepts a space, an NBSP, or one braille cell (U+2800-U+28FF). A pattern requiring a space there matched 0 of 1 live captures and was corrected.

promptGlyph.source: Live capture: U+203A SINGLE RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK, rendered bold (`\x1b[1m›\x1b[0m`), at column 0 of the composer line. Observed identical across gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-6-astra at low/medium/high reasoning effort. Not established as invariant across themes or future versions.

promptPad.source: Live capture: one ordinary space (U+0020) between glyph and first input column, not an NBSP as Claude uses. Confirmed by cursor position — tmux reports cursor_x=2 with the glyph at column 0 on an empty composer, across 12 samples.

placeholderSgr.source: Live capture: the placeholder is emitted as `\u001b[2mAsk Codex to do anything`, i.e. SGR 2 (dim), the same attribute Claude uses. The braille shimmer is NOT outside this field merely because it carries only a truecolor foreground. `_cells` applies SGR sub-parameters as attributes, so `\u001b[38;2;R;G;Bm` records 38, 2 and R — the 2 from the truecolor selector is indistinguishable from a real dim attribute, and a probe confirms `sgr.has(2)` is true for such a cell. The shimmer is therefore handled by `decorativePattern`, which names it explicitly, rather than by this field happening to catch it.

idleMarker.source: Measured from outside the pane over 50 samples at 1.5s intervals against a live codex session: the status row reads `· Ready ·` at rest and `· Working ·` during a turn — present in 45/45 at-rest samples, absent in 5/5 working samples, zero overlap. Required because codex keeps its composer drawn during a turn, so the composer-empty read alone would call a working pane idle. The separators are part of the declared marker on purpose: the gate matches with `includes()` over the whole captured tail, so a bare `Ready` would also be satisfied by ordinary transcript text such as a tool line reading `Ready in 1.2s`, which is not an at-rest signal at all. `· Ready ·` is the status row's own rendering and was confirmed present on the live pane. Known limit, NOT measured: a cold pane that has not yet drawn its status row has no idle marker, and declaring one puts codex on the readiness-gated prime paste (`lib/sessions.js#_awaitPaneReady`). Every sample here was taken on a warm session; a freshly launched codex pane did render the status row with `Ready` in it during startup captures, but the gate's cold-start timing was not measured.

decorativePattern.source: Measured, not predicted. codex paints an animated braille shimmer (U+2800-U+28FF) across the composer line AND the lines above it, continuously, in any session that has conversation history. It broke both idle gates. Movement: `_paneDigest` hashes the transcript region above the composer, where part of the shimmer is drawn — 8 distinct digests over 8 samples of a completely idle pane, so the monitor reported `pane-writing` forever and the nudge could never fire. Composer: a shimmer cell lands between glyph and cursor about a third of the time (8 empty / 4 blocked, reproduced in two independent 12-sample runs), and it OVERWRITES the pad cell, which made the separator unrecognisable. Declaring the range makes both gates discount cells the ENGINE drew rather than the operator; the digest blanks them to spaces rather than deleting them, so a moving shimmer cannot shorten a line and reintroduce the instability. After the fix, on the same live pane: 1 distinct digest over 8 idle samples, composer 12/12 empty, and the wake nudge fired end to end. Scoped to the engine that draws them — claude and antigravity declare nothing, so braille typed into those engines is still input. Accepted cost, stated rather than hidden: braille an operator genuinely types into codex is discounted as decoration. NOT caused by tui.animations, the model, or reasoning effort — a fresh gpt-6-astra high session with animations ON showed zero shimmer over 12 samples, so it tracks session history rather than configuration.
